title: Kaiser's clarinet, saxophone, Louis Dumaine and the nickname
summary: Kaiser learned clarinet by ear in the country, later played saxophone and with every band, including Louis Dumaine's, and was nicknamed Kaiser in World War I.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: That's an old, raggedy car. So when did he start on the clarinet? Was he playing up in the country too, I guess?
He started on a C clarinet. A C? I was down here and I bought a C clarinet and he was playing by air.
He learned down here in New Orleans?
No, he learned in the country. Up in the country?
Up in the country, yeah. But you got the clarinet down here?
Yeah, got the center tuned. And he later on, he played saxophone, that's why he started reading. And it was pretty good. He played with every band in the city pretty much, you know. Yeah.
I know he made those records with Louis Dumaine.
Louis Dumaine, that's right. I used to play with it myself.
Louis Dumaine, there's three of them. Me and my brother here, Nelson Joseph, Kaiser. And the first Kaiser by the name of Louis Joseph. Always Louis Dumaine's band.
Well, it was Kaiser's, was that his second name or how did they call it?
Well, his first name is Willie, his right name is Willie Joseph. Willie Joseph, yes.
Where'd you get that name of Kaiser?
How'd they? Oh, I don't know. During the war, World War I. World War I, they called him Kaiser, you know.
Because some people just call him Willie Kaiser, they don't even call him Willie Joseph.
I thought that was his last name one time.
